## The bets

The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.

Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.

Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.

| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review
### 6. Camera cutout and layouts

**Pitch.** The creator ticks Remove Background on a camera clip. Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background the way Reverse is. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between:

- corner bubble (circle or rounded);
- side by side;
- stacked for vertical;
- camera full;
- screen only.

"Hide camera while silent" fades the camera out during pauses. Text Behind Subject follows from cutout: a title sits between the person and their background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** This is mostly catch-up. Screen Studio 4 (cutout in beta) [S6], Cap 0.6 [S16], Tella [S11], Prequel [S19] and Loom [S13] shipped camera cutout or layouts in September and October 2026. Final Cut Pro [P14], Premiere [P2] and Resolve [P8] ship one-click subject masks. Frame Job's recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. It pulls ahead only in combination: layouts are actions any agent can write, the camera gets Frame Job's grading and LUT engine, and with bet 2 the whole screencast polish lives inside a full editor.

**Builds on.** Issue #124 and its E9 Vision spike; `ReverseRenderer`, `ReverseCache`, `BackgroundRender` and `MediaCacheLedger`; matte tracks (`recipe_matte.rs`); actions over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow; Add Background; the speech spans of the microphone media.

**Effort.** L.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Edge quality on hair is a risk. Balanced person masks are 512×384 and likely need a refinement pass. Accurate masks run at 1.7× realtime and take 1.7 GiB per minute.
- Non-person masks flicker on video, so non-person cutout is for stills only.
- A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and drifts on trims, splits and speed changes. A per-layer mask with a format bump is the sound design.
- Issue #124's `texture(2)` binding is stale: looks now hold texture 2 and curves texture 3.
- The camera clip has no sound of its own, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone's spans through the microphone clip.
- Spec §1's ML non-goal, and issue #124's proposed decision D5, must enter §11 first.
- The 8-decoder budget is a warning, not a refusal. HLG projects need the mask in the right working space.

### The next tier

- **Proposals: play an agent's multi-step edit before it lands (M; Recipes later, also M).** Only Frame Job can do this cheaply. Handles are immutable. The export pin already renders a project that is not the current one. `performGroupedEdit` already makes one undo step from many. An agent's turn becomes a side chain the creator plays and compares A/B with the current cut, then accepts as one named step or rejects. This answers the 44% who want to review or undo and the 37% who want to see what the agent does [D4]. It amends spec §11 AI-10, which accepted ten Undos for a ten-call turn. It matters most once bets 1 and 4 produce agent-driven batches. Recipes come after Proposals and need three things: tool allow-lists enforced by the gate, because a shared recipe is a prompt-injection path; cost shown as an estimate range, because `pricing.ts` prices a run after it happens; and prompts served from `mcp-proxy`, because `core/src/agent.rs` is generic code.
- **Punch in on cuts (S).** Alternates scale between about 100% and 112% across cuts within one take, centred on the face, with `set_video` x, y and scale as one grouped step. It is free and exact, and needs no disclosure. Ship it right after bet 1's first phase.
- **Source ranges, skimming, In and Out, favourite ranges (M).** `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` gain a source range, and `opTool` prints it into the MCP tools automatically. This is the precondition for placing a found moment and for a clean restore in bet 1. Add proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.
- **Caption styles, brand kit and project templates (M).** Colour controls are safe under spec §11 W-10. Size and font changes need re-paging or a W-10 amendment. Per-word emphasis and emoji need a `model_words.rs` field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3. Whether emoji render correctly in HLG projects is unverified.
- **Publish polish slice (S).** A copyable 00:00 chapter list from chapter markers, checked against YouTube's rule [D21]; approximate platform safe-zone overlays [D24]; named platform export targets. Skip AI titles and thumbnails, which YouTube Studio is adding itself [C29].
- **Measure multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback (S).** Bet 5 and any claim to lead depend on it. It is a measurement, not performance work.
- **`search_media` over cached transcripts (S).** The useful slice of a footage index. Build the Vision and Sound Analysis analysis inside bets 3, 4 and 6.
- **Merge the in-app tutorials after TU4 (S).** Creators arriving from CapCut need onboarding. The merge needs TutorialTargets rows for the audio road map.
- **Optical-flow slow motion, spike first (S, then M).** `VTFrameProcessor` accepts only 64RGBAHalf on this Mac, and its handling of HDR encodings is untested. Interpolated smooth cuts across a jump cut stay a spike, not a commitment.
- **WebVTT import (S); translated captions later (M).** A later phase of a caption road map, not a bet.

## Not worth chasing

| Item | Reason |
|---|---|
| Generative media: AI B-roll and video, avatars, voice clones, lip-synced dubbing | Nothing on the device can do it, so it means brokering credit-metered vendor APIs, the model Frame Job competes against. It carries disclosure risk [D25]. YouTube [C26] and Instagram [C28] now dub and translate for free. |
| Direct upload, scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics | An open-source app with no backend cannot keep OAuth client secrets. A shared quota would cap all users together, and posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server. Bring-your-own storage is the only later form that fits. |
| Stock libraries; a template marketplace | These need licensing, curation and a backend. One developer cannot match CapCut's volume [C1] or MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro [P15]. Agent-written graphics and `.fjgraphic` packages are the counter. |
| Eye-contact correction, face retouching | Apple has no public API for these on recorded video. They would need cloud or custom generative face models, with likeness risk and a per-frame cost the one-pass compositor cannot absorb. |
| Cloud sync, collaboration, mobile or iPad apps, Windows | Each needs a backend or a second platform. |
| Remote guest recording, live multi-camera capture | This is Riverside's moat [C9] and needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest files instead, and switch between them with bet 5. |
| A virality score | Creators distrust scored clips [D16]. A stated reason per moment is honest and controllable. |
| A standalone on-device footage index | The major editors shipped footage search within a year [P1] [P13] [P9]. Vision gives only fixed labels, so free-text search needs a bundled model whose licence is unverified. Build slices inside bets 3, 4 and 6, plus `search_media`. |
| Script to cut: a listening teleprompter that assembles takes | Teleprompters are common [S19] [S16]. Script-first recording suits a minority. `SpeechEngine.swift` is file-based today. The valuable kernel, retake removal, belongs in bet 1. |
| Translated captions and soft subtitle tracks as a bet | Platforms translate themselves [C26] [C28]. ADA Title II needs same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. Platforms take the sidecar SRT and VTT files Frame Job already writes. |
| A publish kit as a headline | YouTube Studio is adding AI titles and title and thumbnail tests [C29]. The on-device model's context cannot hold a long transcript, and Frame Job already meets the loudness targets. Only the S slice is worth doing. |
| More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline | MCP became expected in 2026 [C6] [C13] [C21] [P10]. Every creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool anyway. |
| Stabilisation, for now | Phones stabilise in camera, and stabilisation mainly serves handheld vlogs. It is feasible later as a cached render. |
| Live-compositor motion blur | It needs several sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. |
| A plugin system | It contradicts the closed effect vocabulary (spec §11 R5-1, G-1) that preview and export parity and the proof suite rest on. |
| Pro finishing as headline features (Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field) | Resolve and Final Cut Pro own these [P9]. Frame Job's colour and HDR already lead every creator tool. |
| Analytics-driven idea features | The platforms hold the data [C23] [C29]. |

## Decisions for the owner

1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
   - A plugin system: stays out.
3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
   - AI-10, for Proposals.
   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

- **CJ-1 — Spec §1's and §2's non-goals are lifted; lifting one makes it allowed, not

  first bullet and CAM-1).** Lifted: multicam; colour grading beyond per-clip controls (already
  in by GR-1 and its successors); a plugin system; motion blur; stabilisation; optical-flow
  retiming; auto-reframe; ML or heavy pixel work outside the compositor's one pass; any platform
  but macOS; and §2's mouse, keyboard and touch callouts, pointer effects, templates, publishing
  to YouTube or Vimeo, and a stock-media library. `recording.md`'s and CAM-1's "callouts stay
  OUT" no longer hold. What is built is what a road map builds; this road map builds the six
  bets of CJ-2. **Standing as current design until a phase amends one in writing, before its
  code:** G-1 (nothing but a graphic clip's module is scriptable); AU-2's out clause (no
  third-party Audio Unit hosting); R5-1 (effects are closed vocabularies); `recording.md`'s
  "nothing is reconstructed afterwards" and "a recording is ordinary media"; CAM-10 (the
  recorded camera lands in the bottom-right corner); the owner's "not wanted" verdicts (GR-20,
  GR-27…GR-30). Each of those entries gains a one-line "**Noted by CJ-1** (2026-11-01): the
  non-goal it cites is lifted; this decision stands as design." so a reader of the entry is not
  misled. Risk accepted: the spec no longer says what Frame Job will not be, so a request that
  once met a non-goal now meets a road map's scope.
- **CJ-2 — Road map "creator-jobs" builds the survey's six bets in one road map, led by people
  who record themselves talking.** First TX, CU and CO (talking-head and screen tutorials), then
  VR and FC (repurposing to shorts), then SW (video podcasts), in the lanes of "Phases" below.
  The survey is `designs/creator-survey.md`; its next tier and "Not worth chasing" table are not
  in this road map and are neither in nor out. Survey decisions 5, 8 and 10 are asked at the
  phase that needs them.
- **CJ-3 — The key rule: a feature that needs a language model or a cloud model works only when
  the person's key for it is present; without it, its menu items and controls are disabled with
  a tooltip naming the key and where it is set, and its tools refuse in that sentence (owner,
  2026-11-01).** The keys are the Anthropic key (AI-8, Settings ▸ Assistant) and the AssemblyAI
  key (R6-5, Settings ▸ Transcription). There is no on-device fallback: Apple FoundationModels
  is not used, and filler detection stays AssemblyAI's (TR-7 stands). Not "significant AI", and
  never gated: on-device Apple frameworks and the models Frame Job already bundles — Vision, Sound
  Analysis, Speech (`SpeechEngine`), Silero VAD and `AUSoundIsolation`. "Present" is a stored,
  non-empty key or the proof's environment variable, in R6-5's order; whether the key is VALID
  is the service's answer to a request and never decides a control. A result already made with a
  key stays usable without one: R6-16 and R6-21 stand, so a gate disables only what would make

- **CJ-5 — The owner's trial: one real video per lead segment, cut in Frame Job alongside TX,

- **CJ-6 — The build arrangement.** An integration worktree outside the repo

**CJ1's block (the key gate).**

- **CJ-10 — `ModelKeys` is the one gate.** `ModelKeys.swift` holds `ModelKey` (`anthropic`,

  `AssistantConfiguration.didChangeNotification` with change "key" and on
  `SettingsWindowController.didChangeNotification`), `sentence(_:)`, `require(_:)` (throws a

  the tooltip, and clear it again when enabled. Every "is there a key" read moves here; the
  sending sites still read the credential to send it.
- **CJ-11 — One sentence per key, for tooltips, notes and refusals.** "No AssemblyAI API key is
  set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." and "No Anthropic API key is set. Set
  one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." They replace `CloudTranscriber.AccessError`'s and
  `TranscribeSheetController.noKeyNote`'s words and `AssistantSession`'s failure; the
  environment-variable clause leaves the person-facing sentence (the proofs' variables are in
  `docs/developing.md`). R6-17's precedence is unchanged; only the words of its credential arm
  change. The Assistant tab's no-key row keeps its call to action, which is not a disabled
  control.
- **CJ-12 — The keyed table, the dispatch gate and the shipped features.** `ModelKeys.keyed`
  lists each keyed feature: its menu selector (if any), its tools, its key, and whether the tool
  is keyed unconditionally. Dispatch refuses an unconditional keyed tool right after the argument
  gate, before its handler (one line in the frozen `AgentServer.swift`). A conditional tool keeps
  its own refusal in its own precedence, in the sentence from `ModelKeys`. The shipped rows:
  `transcribe_for_fillers` (unconditional); `transcribe` with `engine: "assemblyai"` (conditional,
  R6-16, R6-17); Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… (disabled only when no AssemblyAI key AND no media in
  scope has a current filler transcript — the sheet's Transcribe rows as today); Generate
  Captions' AssemblyAI engine item (disabled, with the tooltip, unless R6-16 would admit the
  batch keyless); the Assistant (its composer and Send as today; View ▸ Assistant stays enabled,
  because the tab is where it says how to set the key; `assistant_send` refuses as today).
- **CJ-13 — The startup parity check gains a sixth part: every keyed tool exists, and its
  catalog description says it needs its key.** In `AgentServer+Parity.swift`; root `CLAUDE.md`'s
  "FIVE parts" becomes six.

**CJ2a's and CJ2b's block (the analysis lane).**

- **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
  state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe. A planner reads it and
  writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
  reversed file is (§5.6). So no analysis kind bumps the format.
- **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, apart from the import lane.** Width 1 unless
  spike CJ-S3 earns 2; `.utility`; its own queue, never the cooperative pool and never
  `MediaCacheLane`. Jobs are wanted by owners — a document's command, a tool call, an export — as
  ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): a job nobody wants is cancelled, one wanted again while it
  runs is not, and `wait` returns on landing, failure or cancellation.
- **CJ-22 — The store.** `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>.json` (plus a payload file where a
  kind needs one), one per media and kind, holding RUNS over source spans in media source ticks:
  a hit is a stored run containing the asked span, a miss runs exactly that span, and the store
  drops the runs the new one contains (TR-14's shape). Written only through
  `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The marker is an `AnalysisStamp`: the source's
  identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind and its version,
  a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS build and the compute device. Any other stamp is a
  miss and the next store replaces the file whole. Coordinates are normalised 0…1 in the media's
  display orientation, origin top-left; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or
  reversal over the file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.
- **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** A kind asks for frames at its own size and rate, in display
  orientation. A media whose picture converts at step 0 (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read through the
  thumbnails' converted path, so analysis sees what the person sees; every other media through a
  scaled `AVAssetReader`. CJ-S3 may move the line.
- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
  Each frame at the media's own rate, read at a long side of 256 px, is reduced to a joint
  colour histogram; a cut is a frame whose distance to the previous one passes the threshold and

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here, before its run. Instruments go in `tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each
run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's
precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the decision named.

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ0; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a project
  hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096, 8,192,
  16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as packages.
  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2) `rc_project_from_json`
  plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times, median; (4) in the Release app
  over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo; (5) the app's resident memory
  after 50 undo steps of `split`. N above 4,096 needs the bench to raise the cap in a scratch
  build only. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms,
  (4) applies in ≤ 1 s and undoes in ≤ 1 s, and (5) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical
  memory. N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision faces on this Mac (at CJ0 when S-TH1 exists, else at CJ3's start; decides
  CJ-30 and CJ-32).** Question: are face tracks deterministic, fast and found on the owner's
  material, and on which device and at what size? Inputs: S-TH1, S-TH2 (V-Log), a portrait iPhone
  file, and the moving-still fixture. Measured: (1) the cache bytes over three runs on each of
  CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; (2) the largest rectangle difference between devices; (3) seconds
  per minute of source at 10 samples a second, frames at long side 720, 1080 and 1440, faces
  alone and with landmarks; (4) the share of samples with a face over S-TH1's first 60 s, which
  its recording brief makes front-facing; (5) on S-TH2, that share on the raw log picture and on
  the converted one; (6) peak memory. **Rules:** the device is the fastest whose three runs are
  byte-identical, else STOP and the kind's stamp carries a tolerance instead of bytes (an
  amendment before CJ3's code); the frame size is the smallest whose face share is within 1
  percentage point of 1440's; the sample rate stays 10 a second if faces with landmarks run at
  ≥ 4× realtime at that size, else 5; landmarks stay in `faces` if they cost ≤ 2× faces alone,
  else mouth opening becomes its own kind, asked only by SW; (4) below 95 % is STOP; (5) picks the
  arm with the higher share, a tie going to the converted picture.
- **CJ-S3 — The lane's reader and width (at CJ2a's start; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23).** Question:
  what does decoding for analysis cost, and does a second concurrent job pay? Measured on a 4K
  HEVC 10-bit file and a 1080p H.264 file: frames a second through the scaled direct reader and
  through the converted path; total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s frames
  composed over 10 s of a 1080p timeline while each runs, against idle. **Rules:** width 2 only
  if two jobs reach ≥ 1.5× one job's throughput AND `play_preview` composes ≥ 95 % of its idle
  count; the converted path only for converting media, unless it is within 10 % of the direct
  reader, when it is used for all.

content.content:
and the tail blends `a → b` over the rest. An identity curve in an END patch
is kept as written and means "animate to neutral" (a `null` there would remove the key,
the rule below); the inspector's Reset inside an action writes it so. The
evaluated end is clamped like every other value, and an identity channel
evaluates to none.

The hue curves (format 20, §11 GR-32), `hue_hue` and `hue_sat`, follow the
same rules in their own units: two of the same count lerp per point (x
linearly, never across 0°/360°); an identity (every value the neutral, the
state writing an absent one as `[[0, 0], [180, 0]]` or `[[0, 1], [180, 1]]`)
meeting a curve of another count takes that curve's x's with the neutral
value; two non-identity hue curves of different counts blend their values
(§11 GR-34), in degrees or as a gain.

**A qualifier's hue centre takes the short way round** (format 18, §11 GR-13):
two present ranges of `video.qualifier` interpolate per number, but a hue
centre is an angle, and 350 → 10 lerped as numbers would sweep through 180.
Before the lerp (`actions_qualifier.rs`), when both states hold a centre more
than 180° apart, the TARGET's centre moves by ±360 (350 → 370), and the
evaluated end's clamp brings the lerped value back into [0, 360) (`rem_euclid
360`): 350 → 10 passes 355, 0, 5. Two centres exactly 180° apart go linearly.
Only the target of the action the time is inside is touched; an ended
action's end is merged as written. A range turned on or off, and `invert`,
switch at the end — a key on one side only holds until then (the object rule
below walks the FROM side's keys). The cleanup blur (format 21, §11 GR-35)
animates whenever both states hold a qualifier: `video_json` writes a
non-neutral qualifier with its `blur` present even at 0
(`actions_qualifier.rs`'s `qualifier_json`), so 0 → 0.5 reads 0.25 halfway; a
qualifier turned on switches at the end.

The object rule is why `text.animation`'s discriminant is spelled `kind`
(format version 5): an action from a typewriter to a line rise switches at
the end, where an action between two typewriters of different lengths
interpolates their `in` and `out`. That second one is legal and rarely what
anybody wants — the two numbers are the animation's own timebase, so
sliding them mid-reveal moves the ground under it — which is a caution, not
a rule the ops enforce.

**`video.motion` is NOT an animation target** (format version 8). A preset is
anchored to the clip's two ends and an action is a ramp between two states,
so there is nothing to interpolate — half a slide into half a spin is not a
picture anybody asked for — and the evaluator would put the base value back
anyway, leaving a control that reported success and did nothing. So
`set_action_end` refuses a patch whose `video` object names `motion`, by
name — the one refusal that is about the OP rather than about the
vocabulary, since the patch is otherwise walked like any other; and

content.content:
- **MT-1 — A matte is a track relation in a closed vocabulary, drawn by the one compositor; R5-1
  and G-1 stand.** A track's `matte` is `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or
  `luma_inverted`, set by `set_track {matte}` (`none` switches it off). A matte track's clips are
  never drawn on the canvas; at each instant what they show cuts every layer the track directly
  behind draws (MT-2). Any clip that draws can be one — text, shape, image, graphic, video, nest.
  Nothing is a package, a shader or an expression, and a graphic on a matte track is called with
  the same arguments and keyed the same way as anywhere (G-5, G-9 untouched). A clip is a matte
  only by the track it is on: moved off, it is ordinary; the tracks `paste` adds are ordinary;
  `duplicate` keeps its track. Persisted as `tracks[].matte`, written only when not `none` — the
  model's first `skip_serializing_if`, so every older file and every ordinary track round-trips
  byte for byte and the reader's default is the same answer. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` 14, no migrate
  step. The video half of #240 is #251 and nothing here decides it.
- **MT-2 — What a matte cuts, and when it cuts nothing.** Its target is the track directly behind
  it in its own container (the timeline, or one nest's own tracks) when that track is not itself
  a matte track. With no such track (the back-most track, or a matte behind it) a matte cuts
  nothing and its clips still draw nothing. Where the matte track shows nothing at an instant — no
  clip, the track hidden, a clip's video off — the track behind shows uncut (owner, 2026-10-07,
  choice 5). Read per instant and per pair of tracks: no clip names another, so split, move,
  delete, paste, nest and undo cannot break a link; `add_track`, `move_track` and `remove_track`
  change which track is behind, visibly. A matte track's clips sound as on any track, and Mute
  Audio silences them (owner, 2026-10-08, O1): a matte is a picture rule, like Hide Video.
- **MT-3 — The four modes, and where the cut is applied.** At a pixel the matte's composite —
  premultiplied, in encoded sRGB like every stage of the compositor (§7.5) — gives: `alpha` its
  alpha a; `alpha_inverted` 1 − a; `luma` the Rec. 709 luma (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, the weights
  the shader's saturation uses) of its premultiplied colour, so transparent counts as black;
  `luma_inverted` 1 − that. The value multiplies the matted layer's coverage at the fragment
  stage's step 7, beside the corner radius and the nest clip rectangle, sampled at the fragment's
  own canvas position. So the matted clip's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape (its
  silhouette pass runs the same stage; owner choice 6), and its reflection is cut by the matte
  where the reflection lands — under an alpha matte, a reflection outside the window is gone — as
  the nest clip rectangle already cuts one (owner, 2026-10-08, O10). The outgoing half of a
  dissolve multiplies its partner's cover by the same value — on one matted track both halves are
  cut by the same matte — which keeps a dissolve under a soft matte exact. `TrackMatte`'s
  declaration order is a shader discriminant (`none` 0 to `luma_inverted` 4): append only.
- **MT-4 — A matte clip's own properties (owner, 2026-10-07, choice 6).** Its placement, crop,
  corner radius, opacity, colour, chroma, filters, spotlight, obscured regions, motion presets,
  actions and transitions with other matte clips shape the matte, because it is drawn by the
  ordinary layer pass. Its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing: the CORE emits a
  matte layer with `blend: "normal"`, `shadow: null` and `reflection: null`, the recipe's second
  deliberate override of model values after a transition's `normal` (§7.3). The inspector shows
  the model's values and says they are not drawn (MT-7). Amends G-10's "blend … apply" for a
  graphic on a matte track.
- **MT-5 — Mattes in nests.** The rule holds in every container. Walking from a layer's own track
  outward through the nest clips it is inside, the first level whose track is a matte track makes
  the layer draw into that matte (or nowhere, when the matte has no target or cuts no layer at
  that instant), and no level outside that applies to the layer; every level inside it whose
  track is a matte's target cuts the layer, each matte multiplying in. One matte is keyed by (the
  ids of the nest clips enclosing its track's container, outermost first — the instance path's
  prefix — and the matte track's id), so two clips showing the same nest at one instant (a split
  nest clip in a dissolve) each have their own matte. A nest clip on a matte track makes its whole
  composite the matte (a matte inside it included), and a nest clip on a matted track has every
  layer it draws cut — at a soft edge, overlapping inner layers show through each other, the
  recorded limit of nest opacity (§7.3). `nest` puts the nest clip on the front-most selected
  track that is not a matte track (the front-most when all are), and gives a nested track its
  source track's matte only when the nested track directly behind it is the copy of that matte's
  target. A selection that takes a matte's clips without its target, beside other clips, is
  nested as asked: the matte clips draw inside the nest and the picture changes; undo restores
  (owner, 2026-10-08, O9). `unnest` lines up the nest's front-most NON-matte track (the
  front-most when all are) with the nest clip's track, so carried matte tracks land on the tracks
  in front of it and nest-then-unnest restores the picture; it makes no track a matte, so a matte
  clip with no track in front lands on a new ordinary track, as any clip refused on the way out
  does.
- **MT-6 — How the compositor draws a matte.** Before the destination pass opens, each matte the
  recipe lists (`mattes`, deepest container first) is drawn by the ordinary layer pipelines into
  a destination-sized `bgra8Unorm` target, so a matte never suspends the destination pass as a
  shadow does. Each distinct set of mattes a layer is cut by is resolved into one
  destination-sized `r8Unorm` coverage texture, cleared to 1, each matte's mode multiplied in by a
  full-frame pass. The layer stage samples it at `texture(1)` at the fragment's
  canvas-normalised position, so Preview Quality, a shadow's canvas-sized silhouette pass, a
  reflection and every export read one coverage. An unmatted layer binds the existing 1×1 white
  placeholder at `texture(1)`, chosen by MT0's spike (2026-10-08; Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1,
  `pmset` powermode 0, on AC power; 200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of the
  runs' medians): one full-bleed unmatted layer (S1) cost 0.014 ms more than the tree's shader
  with the placeholder route and 0.019 ms more with the function-constant route at 1920×1080,
  against a V0-against-V0 noise floor of 0.038 ms, and 0.052 ms and −0.003 ms more at 3840×2160,
  against 0.002 ms — the placeholder within its bound plus the noise at both sizes (0.02 ms at
  1080p, 0.08 ms at 4K). With it a matte cost (S3 − S2, the text as an alpha matte) −0.082 ms at
  1080p, a negative figure larger than that size's noise floor, so the 1080p series do not
  resolve a matte's cost, and 0.066 ms at 4K; two mattes in one coverage (S4 − S2)
  0.040 ms and 0.542 ms, within the 0.50 ms and 2.00 ms budget. Risk accepted: at 4K every
  unmatted full-bleed layer pays 0.05–0.07 ms for the sample (S1: 0.052 ms over the tree's
  shader; two layers, S2: 0.887 ms with the placeholder against 0.752 ms with the function
  constant), for one pipeline per layer
  specialization instead of two. `LayerUniforms` stays 104 floats. Targets are pooled per destination
  size and allocated on the first matted frame (at 3840×2160, 33.2 MB per matte and 8.3 MB per
  coverage). (Amended by PR-1: each matte's composite is `rgba16Float`, 66.4 MB at 3840×2160;

- **MT-7 — The chrome (owner, 2026-10-08, O2–O8).** No fifth header toggle and no shortcut. Set

content.content:
reverb given mono aborts the process; an `AVAudioPlayerNode`; schedule →
`start()` → `play()`; fixed 4,096-frame calls; presets through
`auAudioUnit.currentPreset`; every parameter set and clamped; a unit removed
rather than set to wet 0; no TimePitch at 0 semitones; float CAF; per-kind
makeup gain.

Tails are cut at the clip end. `CompositionBuilder` substitutes the file per
clip, and plays DRY while a render is pending.

### E9 — Remove Background (orig §6 E9, §5b; D5)

`video.cutout` is `{subject: person|foreground, feather}`.

`person` uses `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` at `.balanced`, with a
FRESH request per frame. `.fast` is stateful; `.accurate` runs at 1.7×
realtime and needs 1.7 GiB per minute; `foreground` applies to images and
stills only.

A new `MediaImporter+Masks.swift` computes 10 masks per second of source,
only for the windows that clips show. They are written as 8-bit PNGs under
`cache/masks/<media>-<subject>/`, made from the CODED buffer. The compute
device is pinned in the marker, and proofs compare against the cached masks,
never a recomputation.

**"No subject" rule, per CLIP WINDOW:** if no mask has at least 0.5 % of its
pixels above 127, the clip draws UNCUT.

In the compositor: the core emits `source_t`; Swift binds the nearest mask
as `texture(2)`, sampled through `orientedUV`; the mask multiplies coverage
at step 7; a frame whose mask is pending draws uncut.

## What it built: where it lives now

- **`tools/proof/effects_spike/`:** the E0 instruments, `fx_*.swift` for
  voice and `vision_*.swift` for segmentation. The README has the build
  lines and fixtures.
- **E1 (road map 5):** `core/src/edit_transition.rs`,
  `core/src/audio_crossfade.rs`, `app/Sources/VideoPane+Transition.swift`,
  `AgentCatalog+Transitions.swift`, `AgentServer+Transitions.swift`,
  `tools/proof/e1_proof.py` and `e1_chrome.py`.
- **E2 (road map 5):** `core/src/model_motion.rs`, `core/src/motion.rs`,
  `core/src/edit_split.rs` (the split rule for motion and
  `text.animation`), `app/Sources/VideoPane+Motion.swift`,
  `MotionProps.swift`, `EditorViewController+Motion.swift`,
  `tools/proof/e2_proof.py` and `e2_chrome.py`.
- **E3–E9:** nothing exists. `flip_x`, `exposure`, `LookKind`, `VoiceKind`,
  `MaskShape`, `cutout` and `.cube` appear nowhere in `core/src` or
  `app/Sources`.

## Known limits

**Architecture a deferred phase will meet** (orig §3, re-checked
2026-09-26): `LayerUniforms` has an empty tail, and `phase8_chrome.py:3259`
asserts 416; a layer samples one texture, and there is no time or seed
uniform; output is confined to the layer's quad, so glow and aberration
cannot bleed past it; there is no previous frame; there is one PreEffects
tap per track; file sizes have moved since orig §3; measure with `wc -l` and read
the file-history ADRs' "Named next cuts" before paying a toll.

**Wipes are measured in each layer's own box**, so a different-size pair
does not meet at one edge (spec §7.5). A canvas-space wipe was withdrawn
because it broke the common same-size pair, nested wipes, and vertical wipes
over a reflection. The right measure, the pair's union box, was left for
later.

**E0 spike numbers — do not re-measure them blind.**

Voice (§5a): Offline rendering works synchronously. It is byte-identical
across engines, processes and concurrent runs, but only at a fixed call
size; a window render is not a slice of a whole-file render: TimePitch
differs by up to +0.34 dBFS; a 10 s window re-renders in 50–270 ms; reverb
tails run 11 ms (smallRoom) to 5.79 s (cathedral); no preset band-limits,
and no preset makes a robot; distortion presets add +0.9 to +19 dB RMS.

Vision (§5b): Calls are synchronous and need no TCC grant; person masks are
always 4:3: fast 256×192, balanced 512×384, accurate 2016×1512; balanced
runs at 4.2–5.5× realtime at 10 masks/s, about 16 MB of PNG per minute;
output is byte-identical on one device, but GPU and ANE differ by up to 25
levels; person coverage is 0.00 % on UI, text and cards; foreground on video
flips up to 57 % of pixels between masks 0.1 s apart; person segmentation
misses backlit, from-behind and small figures.

Not measured: audible quality; multi-track or variable-rate `.mov` audio
through `AVAudioFile`; an `AVComposition` playing a cached CAF; the
first-ever Neural Engine compile; masks on real camera footage, or across
machines and OS versions.

content.content:
- **CAM-10 — A camera beside the screen lands, and `record_screen` records it (CR3b), recorded before its code; amends CAM-4 (2), CAM-6 (6) and CAM-9 (10).** A screen recording's `(Camera).mov` files (CAM-9) land in the same grouped edit as its movies and microphone files, and the tool admits `camera` and `camera_format` with source `screen`. CAM-3 to CAM-9 stand except where this entry amends them. 1. **The track.** ONE new track at the open container's FRONT (its index is the container's track count after the pictures have landed), named "Camera", added on the attempt of the first camera clip that takes a frame and kept only when that clip lands (`addMicrophones`' attempt pattern), so a recording none of whose camera files makes a clip adds no track. 2. **Time.** Segment k's camera clip is asked at `screenStart_k + cameraOffset_k`, its floor `max(screenStart_k, the previous camera clip's end)`. A start below the floor is head-trimmed to it by the microphone's shared dance (`headTrimmed`: add at the floor, `trim_start`, move back, read back, a second try a frame up at an inexact rate). CR3a measured every `cameraOffset` negative, so the trim is the usual path. A camera wholly under its head lands as media only with " was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of it would remain after the ms head that keeps it clear of ." A screen picture that minted no clip still gives its `at`. A segment LEFT OUT because its screen movie would not probe (`UnreadableSegment`) keeps its camera file on disk, named in `kept_files` and its left-out sentence (CAM-9 (7)), and never lands it; only its microphone takes the slot (#181 item 2), so the camera's starts are read off the `.segment(k)` stretches alone. 3. **The corner.** With the container's canvas `cw × ch` (inside an open nest, the nest's) and the camera file's `sw × sh`: `s = clamp(min(0.25·cw/sw, ch/(3·sh)), 0.01, 10)` — the box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, the core's scale range — `x = (cw/2 − 0.05·cw − sw·s/2).rounded()` and `y = (ch/2 − 0.05·ch − sh·s/2).rounded()`, in the C frame (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`: an offset of the layer's centre from the canvas centre, y down). So the picture sits in the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, inside the 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas (the guide spec §4.1 names title-safe; the industry's action-safe). One `set_video {x, y, scale}` per clip, right after its placement; nothing else is set, and the clip stays an ordinary clip a person moves. 4. **One grouped edit**, in the order pictures → cameras → microphones. `place: false` lands the camera media with no clip and no track. A new project lands the cameras through `remainderPlacement`, after the later pictures; without clip 1, as media only with its `unplacedNote`. For ONE segment that undo step is "Add Camera and Microphone" with a camera and any voice (its own or a left-out segment's), "Add Camera" with a camera alone, and otherwise as before ("Add Microphone", "Add Recording Segments"). 5. **The tool.** `camera` and `camera_format` are admitted with source `screen`, lifting CAM-4 (2) and CAM-6 (6) for it. With source screen, a `camera_format` given without `camera` is refused in CAM-4 (2)'s step (3): "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen." With source voice_over the given ones of `camera`, `camera_format` are refused there together: "With source voice_over, cannot be given — a voice-over records the microphone alone." (CAM-4 (2)'s "only source camera records a camera" is no longer true.) The order after step (5): (6) `project`; (7) the camera lookup and its format — for a screen recording too, when `camera` is given; (8) the Camera grant; then, for a screen, the Screen Recording grant and the display or window lookup; (9) the recording. The tool never prepares a capture or adopts one (CAM-7 (7)). 6. **The answer.** Per `segments[k]` and never at the top level: `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` when that segment has a camera file; `camera_problem` and `camera_note` when set; `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known. The top-level `camera` is CAM-4 (6)'s, unchanged. `note` gains every segment's `cameraProblem` then `cameraNote`, in order, after `camera.problem` and `camera.note`. 7. **The stop wait** counts three probes per segment with a camera beside the screen (`finishCeiling + 3 × probeTimeout × max(n, 1) + 5`), and its timeout sentence names the camera files after the movies (" Its camera file is at ." / " Its camera files are at , ."), read from the recorder's held camera paths. 8. **The readers.** With a camera BESIDE the screen the panel's landing note says the display's `.systemStopped` sentence (not the camera's) and puts `camera.problem` after the microphone's problem; every segment's `cameraProblem` and `cameraNote` lead the placement's notes, and follow `camera.note` in a failed landing's note. `filesClause` adds " and its camera at

" or " and its camera files at , " after the microphone clause. 9. **No panel door yet.** The recorder panel offers no camera with a screen source until CR3c (CAM-11); until then the tool is the one door that records a camera beside the screen. - **CAM-11 — The panel's camera beside the screen (CR3c), recorded before its code; amends CAM-5 (2), CAM-6 (2), CAM-7 (1) and (3), and CAM-10 (7) and (9).** With a display or the Window row chosen, the recorder panel offers a "Record the camera too" checkbox; ticked, the panel records the chosen camera at the chosen format beside the screen (CAM-9, CAM-10). CAM-3 to CAM-10 stand except where this entry amends them. 1. **The box** is a grid row with no label, directly under Include Frame Job windows and above Camera. It is enabled only while idle with a display row or the Window row; under Camera or Microphone Only it is greyed with its value kept. It is a control of its own: an "Off" row in the Camera popup would change what the shared camera key means for Source Camera and for hot-plug (CAM-8). 2. **The key.** `FrameJobRecordingCameraBeside`, a Bool, off when absent, is written by `persistChoices` on every change and read by `restoreChoices`. It persists across launches, unlike the session-only Camera row; it is the panel's tenth `FrameJobRecording…` key, pinned in the harness and `screens.py`. A hot-plug writes nothing (CAM-8 (4)). 3. **A camera wanted** means Source Camera, or the box ticked with a display row or the Window row. Then the Camera and Format popups are live while idle (amending CAM-5 (2) and CAM-6 (2)'s "only while idle with Source Camera"). `currentChoice()` carries `camera` (the popup's id) and `cameraFormat` (nil for Best) beside a `.display` or `.picked` source; otherwise `camera` is nil, as before. With the box ticked, System Audio, Show Clicks, Size, Include Frame Job windows and Rate stay live, and the size note is the screen's. 4. **The preview** (amending CAM-7 (1) and (3)). The well's row is shown, and CAM-7's step runs, whenever a camera is wanted; step (1) reads "the panel not visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off". Step (2) also covers a screen recording's camera beside it: that capture's layer, else "The camera is recording.". `prepareCamera` acts for any choice naming a camera whose source is not `.voiceOver`. The countdown keeps that capture, and the panel's `start(…, mayAsk: true)` adopts it (CAM-9 (1)); a tool start never does (CAM-7 (7)). 5. **The press with the box ticked**, in order: (1) Window… with nothing picked gives its sentence; (2) no camera gives "No camera is connected."; (3) the Screen Recording grant; (4) the Camera grant, asked from `notDetermined`, `Privacy_Camera` opened when denied or restricted, and a prompt's answer re-read before the microphone is checked (CAM-5 (4)); (5) the Microphone grant; (6) the countdown. With the box off nothing changes, and the Camera grant is never read. 6. **The recording** is a screen recording: the panel orders out (`hidesForRecording` unchanged), the status item is its chrome, and it lands by CAM-10. 7. **The timeout sentence** (amending CAM-10 (7)) spells the ceiling the stop wait used — its `camera:` is the wait's own `cameraBeside` — even when the recorder holds no camera file. 8. **CAM-10 (9) is lifted.** The box is the panel's door to a camera beside the screen, and the catalog's `record_screen` description and the guide name it.

content.content:
- **Accessibility is never asked for**, and Frame Job never posts an event.
  - **No Info.plist key or entitlement**, unless spike CU-S1 measures one is needed. CU-S1 also
    records whether a relaunch is needed after the grant.
- **CU-4 — The cursor is part of its clip's layer, not a clip of its own.**
  - The compositor draws the cursor and its ripples into the layer's SOURCE texture, after
    step 0 and before crop, placement, colour, filters, spotlight, obscure, matte and
    transition. A burned-in cursor met all of those, so the picture keeps parity with one.
    It follows every transform, zoom action, nest and speed ramp the clip has.
  - A sprite on another track would drift on the first trim, slip or speed change, which is
    why it is not one.
  - The core computes the cursor's source time and its state.
  - The compositor only draws.
- **CU-5 — Planners live in the core, and their results are ordinary ops.** Auto zoom,
  shortcut overlays and typing stretches are pure functions of the cursor file and the
  project. Each answers a list of existing ops (and CU9's one new op), which Swift applies as
  one named undo step.
  - **No action or clip is tagged "generated."** There is no format change for it.
  - **Re-planning finds zooms by content.** It recognises a zoom action by the core's twin of
    `ActionBands.isZoom` (CU7). A probe row holds the two tests to one answer.
- **CU-6 — The spikes' rules are fixed before their runs.** These are the rules under
  "Spikes", below.
  - Each instrument stores this file's SHA-256 as `rule_sha256` in its `results.json`, as
    CAM-2 did.
  - A spike's verdict is recorded here before the phase that depends on it starts.
- **CU-7 — Keys are private by construction.**
  - **Never during secure input.** Nothing is recorded while `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` is
  - **Z5.** `isZoom` and `action_is_zoom` agree on 12 fixture ends (probe).
  - **Z6.** Undo removes every action in one step.
- **Mutants:**
  - the merge gap ignored;
  - the region not clamped;
  - clip time without S;
  - Replace removing non-zoom actions;
  - the lead applied after the click.
- **Manual check:** JOB-6. Auto Zoom on the owner's real tutorial: are the zooms where a person
  would put them? This is a verdict, carried into CU12.
- **Depends on:** CU5 (media link, `get_cursor_events`), CU2.

content.content:
- **R5-3 — `add_transition` builds the overlap from handles, clamps the
  duration, and never moves a third clip.** A shorter transition is the
  same edit at a size the media allows; a gap closed part-way
  (`close_gap`'s refusal) is a different edit. Not being at a hard cut is a
  wrong ARGUMENT (`Err`), because the op is pointed at one cut by a caller
  who meant that cut — unlike `roll`, which a drag can reach at any edge;
  having no handle is a domain refusal (`Outcome::Refused`, §5.5 — it
  says so in its own sentence since road map 7's D2·3).
  **Amended 2026-09-16, by the user: when there is no handle, OFFER to
  shift.** Two whole files placed back to back — the most common screencast
  cut — have no handle on either side, so the rule above left Clip ▸
  Transition ▸ with nothing to do but refuse. `add_transition` gained
  `ripple`, and the refusal sheet a button that sends it: the incoming clip
  and everything at or after the cut on every unlocked track slide left, the
  timeline gets shorter, and the tracks stay in sync (the user chose
  "everything after", over "the rest of this track" and "just the clip").
  The rule above still holds for the default form, which is still what the
  menu tries first: a third clip moves only when a person has been told it
  will and said yes, or an agent passed `ripple` by name.
- **R5-4 — Motion is a presentation term.** `video.motion` is stored in the
  model and drawn by the recipe, but `evaluate_clip`, `get_project`, the
  inspector's fields and every edit read the clip un-moved. It is the
  second place the recipe draws what the model does not say — the first
  being the forced `normal` blend under a transition (§7.3). It is not an
  animation target: an action cannot animate it, and a file that tries is
  drawn with the base motion.
- **R5-5 — Motion is a pure function of clip time.** No seed, no wall
  clock, no previous frame: `render_frame` at a tick is byte-identical run
  after run, preview and export agree, and two clips with the same preset
  at the same clip time are displaced identically.

content.content:
`MediaCacheLoader`, the cache posts and `CacheLedger`'s per-file passes take the key.
- **SW-41 — Which sources are made.** Every media with audio gets its default source, first, as
  today. Any other source is made when a clip of the project, in any container, plays it, after
  the default source and in stream order. A source no clip plays any more is pruned at the next
  pass, as a stale cache is.
- **SW-42 — Speech spans per source (format 39p; amends AU-110).** `media.speech` stays the
  default source's. `media.audio_speech` is `[{stream, channel?, spans}]` for any other source,
  one entry per source, written only when non-empty. `set_media_speech` takes `stream` and
  `channel` (defaults 0 and none). AU-116's relink rule clips or clears each entry.

**SW5 — OBS's Matroska.**
- **SW-50 — The rewrap copies every audio track (amends #216-R).** Draft: "Amended by SW-50:
  Swift copies the first video stream and EVERY audio stream, in the file's order, each with its
  Name, unchanged; `required_bytes` counts them all; a track whose codec the copy does not carry
  sends the whole file to the opt-in ffmpeg step as before."
- **SW-51 — `rc_container_sample`'s track argument is an index**: 0 the video, 1 + k the k-th
  audio track; `describe` lists the audio tracks as an array. Three files in lockstep.
- **SW-52 — The ffmpeg step maps every audio stream** (`-map 0:a?`), amending #216-R's ffmpeg
  sentence.

**SW6 — a channel as a source.**
  changes. "Make a copy" is a checkbox, ticked by default and never remembered.
- **VR-31 — The copy opens with the step as its one undo step**, "Make Vertical Version", so Undo in
  the copy shows the 16:9 copy. It is named "<source name> (9:16)" or "(1:1)".
- **VR-32 — Shapes and sizes.** 9:16 and 1:1, keeping the source canvas's short side and even: from
  1920 × 1080 they are 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. A shape equal to the current canvas is not
  offered. 4:5 is asked at VR3.
- **VR-33 — Which clips are followed.** A top-level media, still or image clip whose rect at its
  first frame spans one whole axis of the canvas (within 1 px) and is centred within 2 % on the
  other is followed with `subject`. A pillarboxed 4:3 or a letterboxed scope picture counts. Every
  other visual top-level clip is `keep`: a camera bubble, a picture-in-picture, a title, a shape,
  a non-full graphic. A full-frame nest clip is `center`. Matte pairs and rotated clips are `keep`
  and are listed.
- **VR-34 — The order of the step.**
  1. `set_canvas {width, height}` with no rescale.
  2. `add_track` at index 0, named "Backgrounds".
  3. `reframe_clip` per visual top-level clip with `from_width`/`from_height` the old canvas and
  video pass under the same key would cancel or queue behind the audio passes.
- `MediaImporter.swift` (589) holds the import's `async` and is at the cap. A video pass started
  by a command needs neither.
- The speech cache is computed at import ("never computed at feature time", `silence.md` :21).
  Video analysis costs far more per second, so VR-10 computes it when a command asks.
- These needs are shared with bet 6 (person masks) and bet 5 (mouth activity for one-camera
  shows), so they are **CJ1, a shared phase**. VR1 is the first pass to run on its lane. What VR
  needs from CJ1:
  - **A video analysis lane.** It runs on its own `.utility` queue, never the cooperative pool
    (#367's rule), at width 1 until VR-S1 measures 2. It is separate from the audio lane, so the
    two never wait on each other.
